body.text: Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā
body.translated_text: <s>Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Wisdom in Ten Thousand Lines)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam: ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭaparvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham anekair bhikṣusahasraiḥ, sarvair arhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravair niṣkleśair vaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair ājāneyair mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyair apahṛtabhārair anuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptair, ekaṃ pudgalaṃ sthāpayitvā yadutāyuṣmantam ānandaṃ śaikṣaṃ srotaāpannaṃ; pañcamātraiś ca bhikṣuṇīśatair, upāsakair upāsikābhiś ca sārdhaṃ, sarvair dṛṣṭasatyair; anekasahasraiś ca bodhisattvair mahāsattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ, sarvair dhāraṇīpratilabdhaiḥ samādhipratilabdhaiḥ śūnyatāvihāribhir animittagocarair avikalpitapraṇidhānaiḥ samatākṣāntipratilabdhair asaṃgapratibhāṇapratilabdhaiḥ sarvaiś ca pañcābhijñair ādeyavacanair akuhakair apagatajñānārthalābhasatkāracittair nirāmiṣadharmadeśakair gambhīradharmakṣāntipāragatair vaiśāradyaprāptair mārakarmasamatikrāntaiḥ sarvakaraṇāvaraṇavimuktair dharmanirdeśasaṃcitair asaṃkhyeyakalpasamārabdhapraṇidhānaiḥ smitamukhaiḥ pūrvābhilāpibhir vyapagatabhrūkuṭīmukhair anantapariṣadabhibhavanavaiśāradyasamanvāgatair anekakalpakoṭinirdeśaniḥsaraṇakuśalair māyāmarīcisvapnodakacandrapratibhāsākāśagandharvanagarapratibimbanirmāṇopamadharmādhimuktair apramāṇavaiśāradyasamanvāgataiḥ sarvasattvacittagatyadhimuktiparyāptikuśalaiḥ sarvasattvāpratihatacittair mahākṣāntisamanvāgatair yāthātmyāvatāraṇakuśalair anantabuddhakṣetravyūhaparigṛhītair asaṃkhyeyalokadhātugatabuddhānusmṛtisamādhisatatasamitābhimukhībhūtair aparimitabuddhādhyeṣaṇakuśalair nānādṛṣṭisamutthitakleśapraśamanakuśalaiḥ samādhivikrīḍanaśatasahasranirhārakuśalais, tadyathā bhadrapālena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, ratnākareṇa ca, sārthavāhena ca, naradattena ca, varuṇadattena ca, indradattena ca, udāramatinā ca, viśeṣamatinā ca, vardhamānamatinā ca, amoghadarśinā ca, susaṃprasthitena cam, suvikrāntavikramiṇā ca, nityodyuktena ca, anikṣiptadhureṇa ca, ādityagarbheṇa ca, candragarbheṇa ca, anupamamatinā ca, avalokiteśvareṇa ca, mañjuśriyā ca, ratnamudrāhastena ca, nityotkṣiptahastena ca bodhisattvena, maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, evaṃpramukhair anekabodhisattvasahasraiḥ, sarvaiḥ kumārabhūtaiḥ sārdham.
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard: At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of monks, with many thousands of monks—all of them <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones) with outflows exhausted, free from defilements, self-mastered, with minds well-liberated, with wisdom well-liberated, thoroughbreds, great elephants, who had done what was to be done, accomplished their task, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, with the fetters of existence completely destroyed, with minds well-liberated through right knowledge, having attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states—with the exception of one person, namely the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, a learner who had attained the stage of stream-entry; and with some five hundred nuns, and with male and female lay followers, all of whom had seen the truths; and together with many thousands of <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> (great beings of awakening)—all of whom had attained <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (mystic formulas), attained <s>samādhis</s> (meditative concentrations), dwelt in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), had the signless as their domain, had undifferentiated aspirations, had attained the patience of equality, had attained unobstructed eloquence, and all possessed the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), whose words were to be accepted, who were without deception, whose minds had abandoned concern for knowledge, gain, honor, and material offerings, who taught the <s>Dharma</s> without material motivation, who had gone to the far shore of patience regarding the profound <s>Dharma</s>, who had attained fearlessness, who had transcended the works of <s>Māra</s>, who were liberated from all obstructive actions, who had accumulated teachings of the <s>Dharma</s>, whose aspirations had been initiated over incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (eons), who were smiling-faced, who spoke first in greeting, whose faces were free from frowning, who possessed the fearlessness of overcoming infinite assemblies, who were skilled in teaching and emerging from instruction over many billions of <s>kalpas</s>, who were devoted to the <s>Dharma</s> as being like illusions, mirages, dreams, reflections of the moon in water, echoes, space, cities of <s>gandharvas</s>, reflected images, and magical creations, who possessed immeasurable fearlessness, who were skilled in understanding the mental dispositions and inclinations of all beings, whose minds were unobstructed toward all beings, who possessed great patience, who were skilled in penetrating the true nature of things, who had embraced the adornment of infinite <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields), who were constantly and continuously face-to-face with the <s>samādhi</s> of recollection of the <s>Buddhas</s> throughout innumerable world-systems, who were skilled in requesting instruction from immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s>, who were skilled in pacifying the defilements arising from various views, who were skilled in bringing forth hundreds of thousands of playful <s>samādhis</s>—namely, with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, <s>Ratnākara</s>, <s>Sārthavāha</s>, <s>Naradatta</s>, <s>Varuṇadatta</s>, <s>Indradatta</s>, <s>Udāramati</s>, <s>Viśeṣamati</s>, <s>Vardhamānamati</s>, <s>Amoghadarśin</s>, <s>Susaṃprasthita</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikramin</s>, <s>Nityodyukta</s>, <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>, <s>Ādityagarbha</s>, <s>Candragarbha</s>, <s>Anupamamati</s>, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Nityotkṣiptahasta</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>—foremost among them, together with many thousands of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all of whom were in the stage of princes.

body.text: tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavān śakraṃ ca brahmāṇaṃ ca sarvāṃś ca lokapālān tejasābhibhūya tāsāṃ catasṛnāṃ parṣadāṃ purato virocamāna ṛddhyā nānāvidhaṃ vikurvaṇaprātihāryaṃ saṃdarśayati sma. romakūpebhyo 'nekāni raśmikoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ.
body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, overpowering <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and all the world-guardians with his radiance, shining before those four assemblies, displayed various kinds of miraculous feats through his supernatural power. From his hair-pores issued forth many billions of hundreds of thousands of rays of light.

body.text: tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān śāradvatīputras tasyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ. sa tathāgatasyedṛśam ṛddhivikurvaṇaprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanaḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāta utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avocat: sacen me bhagavān praśnavyākaraṇāyāvakāśaṃ kuryād ahaṃ bhagavantam kaṃcit pradeśaṃ prakṣyāmi.
body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (Śāriputra) had assembled and was seated in that assembly. Having seen such a miraculous feat of supernatural power by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he was delighted, elated, joyful, glad, and filled with happiness and satisfaction. Rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms in the direction of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "If the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity for asking a question and receiving an answer, I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about a certain matter."

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram etad avocat: tathāgataṃ praṣṭuṃ, śāradvatīputra, sadā kṛtāvakāśatvād yat kiṃcit tvaṃ tathāgataṃ praṣṭum icchasi, tat prccha, praśnaprativacanena cāhaṃ tava cittam ārādhayiṣye.
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, since the opportunity to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s> is always available, whatever you wish to ask the <s>Tathāgata</s>, ask it, and through the answer to your question I shall satisfy your mind."

body.text: evam ukta āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantam etad avocat: prajñāpāramitā, bhadanta bhagavan, prajñāpāramitety ucyate; katamā bhadanta bhagavan sā bodhisattvānaṃ prajñāpāramitā? kasya dharmasya pāramitāyāṃ bodhisattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pāraṃ gatāḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante?
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, is spoken of as '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' What, O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattvas</s>? Through the perfection of which <s>dharma</s> have the <s>bodhisattvas</s> gone to the far shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and quickly attained <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening)?"

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmate śāradvatīputrāya sādhukāram adāt: sādhu, sādhu, śāradvatīputra, yat tvaṃ tathāgatasyādhiṣṭhānād evaṃ praśnaṃ pṛcchasi, sādhu; sundaras te saṃkalpaḥ, tena hi tvaṃ śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ prajñāpāramitām.
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave his approval to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, that you ask such a question through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Excellent! Your intention is beautiful. Therefore, listen, and attend well and carefully—I shall speak about the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>."

body.text: evam astu bhadanta bhagavann ity āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavataḥ pratyaśroṣīt.
body.translated_text: "So be it, venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>," the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> replied to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: bhagavāṃs tasyaitad avocat: śāradvatīputra prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramitety ucyate yad idaṃ sarvadharmānabhiniveśaḥ. anabhiniviṣṭāḥ śāradvatīputra bodhisattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pāraṃ gatāḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: "<s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is spoken of as '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' because it is the non-grasping of all <s>dharmas</s>. <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are non-grasping have gone to the far shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and quickly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>."

body.text: āha: katame bhadanta bhagavaṃs te sarvadharmā yeṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anabhiniviṣṭāḥ?
body.translated_text: He asked: "What, O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, are all those <s>dharmas</s> with regard to which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are non-grasping?"

body.text: bhagavān āha: sarvadharmāḥ śāradvatīputrocyante yaduta pañca skandhā, dvādaśāyatanāny, aṣṭādaśa dhātavaś, catvāry āryasatyāni, dvādaśa pratītyasamutpādāṅgāni, catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāṇi, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāny, āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaḥ, śūnyatāvimokṣamukham, animittavimokṣamukham, apraṇihitavimokṣamukhaṃ, catvāri dhyānāni, catvāry apramānāni, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayo, 'sṭau vimokṣā, daśānupūrvavihārasamāpattayo, nava saṃjñā, daśānusmṛtayaḥ, ṣaṭ saṃjñākārā, dharmajñānam, anvayajñānaṃ, paracittajñānani, saṃvṛtijñānaṃ, duḥkhajñānaṃ, samudayajñānaṃ, nirodhajñānaṃ, mārgajñānaṃ, kṣayajñānam, anutpādajñānaṃ, yathābhūtajñānaṃ ca; evam eva savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhir, avitarko vicāramātraḥ samādhir, avitarkāvicāraḥ samādhir, anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam, ājñendriyam, ājñātāvīndriyam, aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni, daśa kṛtsnāyatanāny, aṣṭādaśa śūnyatā, daśa tathāgatabalāni, catvāri vaiśāradyāni, catasraḥ pratisaṃvido, mahāmaitrī, mahākaruṇā, aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāś ca; evam eva sarvajñatā, mārgākārajñatā, sarvākārajñatā, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ, pañcābhijñāḥ, pañca cakṣūṃṣi, dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāny, aśītir anuvyañjānāni ca. ete te sarvadharmā yeṣv anabhiniviṣṭā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pāraṃ gatāḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are said to be: namely, the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the four <s>āryasatyas</s> (noble truths), the twelve links of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), the five <s>balas</s> (powers), the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the noble eightfold path, the <s>śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha</s> (door of liberation through emptiness), the <s>animitta-vimokṣamukha</s> (door of liberation through signlessness), the <s>apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha</s> (door of liberation through wishlessness), the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the four formless attainments, the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), the ten successive abiding attainments, the nine perceptions, the ten <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections), the six aspects of perception, knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>, inferential knowledge, knowledge of others' minds, conventional knowledge, knowledge of suffering, knowledge of origination, knowledge of cessation, knowledge of the path, knowledge of destruction, knowledge of non-arising, and knowledge of things as they truly are; likewise, <s>samādhi</s> with applied and sustained thought, <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought but with sustained thought only, <s>samādhi</s> without applied or sustained thought, the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the faculty of complete knowledge, the faculty of one who has fully known, the eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery), the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases), the eighteen kinds of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>; likewise, <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), <s>mārgākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of path-aspects), <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the five eyes, the thirty-two marks of a great person, and the eighty secondary characteristics. These are all those <s>dharmas</s> with regard to which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, being non-grasping, have gone to the far shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and quickly attain <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text: tata āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantam etad avocat: katame bhadanta bhagavan pañca skandhāḥ, peyālaṃ yāvat katamāni dvādaśa pratītyasamutpādāṅgāni, katamāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, peyālaṃ yāvat katama āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaḥ, katamaṃ śūnyatāvimokṣamukhaṃ, peyālaṃ yāvat sarvākārajñatā, katamāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ, peyālaṃ yāvad aśītir anuvyañjanāni?
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "What, O venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the five <s>skandhas</s>? And so on in abbreviated form, up to: what are the twelve links of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? What are the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>? And so on in abbreviated form, up to: what is the noble eightfold path? What is the door of liberation through <s>śūnyatā</s>? And so on in abbreviated form, up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? What are the six <s>pāramitās</s>? And so on in abbreviated form, up to the eighty secondary characteristics?"

body.text: [DsP_1] evam ukte bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram etad avocat: pañca skandhā iti, śāradvatīputra, ucyante yaduta rūpaṃ, vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā, vijñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_1] Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "The five <s>skandhas</s>, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are said to be: namely, <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)."

body.text: [DsP_2] tatra katamāni dvādaśāyatanāni? ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāni, ṣaḍ bāhyāni. etāny ucyante dvādaśāyatanāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_2] Therein, what are the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases)? Six internal and six external. These are called the twelve <s>āyatanas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamāni ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni? yaduta cakṣurāyatanaṃ, śrotrāyatanaṃ, ghrāṇāyatanaṃ, jihvāyatanaṃ, kāyāyatanaṃ, manaāyatanam. etāny ucyante ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni.
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the six internal <s>āyatanas</s>? Namely: the eye-base (<s>cakṣur-āyatana</s>), the ear-base (<s>śrotra-āyatana</s>), the nose-base (<s>ghrāṇa-āyatana</s>), the tongue-base (<s>jihvā-āyatana</s>), the body-base (<s>kāya-āyatana</s>), and the mind-base (<s>mana-āyatana</s>). These are called the six internal <s>āyatanas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamāni ṣaḍ bāhyāny āyatanāni? yaduta rūpāyatanaṃ, śabdāyatanaṃ, gandhāyatanaṃ, rasāyatanaṃ, spraṣṭavyāyatanaṃ, dharmāyatanam. etāny ucyante ṣaḍ bāhyāny āyatanāni.
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the six external <s>āyatanas</s>? Namely: the form-base (<s>rūpa-āyatana</s>), the sound-base (<s>śabda-āyatana</s>), the smell-base (<s>gandha-āyatana</s>), the taste-base (<s>rasa-āyatana</s>), the touch-base (<s>spraṣṭavya-āyatana</s>), and the dharma-base (<s>dharma-āyatana</s>). These are called the six external <s>āyatanas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_3] tatra katama aṣṭādaśa dhātavaḥ? yaduta cakṣurdhātū, rūpadhātuś, cakṣurvījñānadhātuḥ; śrotradhātuḥ, śabdadhātuḥ, śrotravijñānadhātuḥ; ghrānadhātur, gandhadhātur, ghrāṇavijñānadhātuḥ; jihvādhātū, rasadhātur, jihvāvijñānadhātuḥ; kāyadhātuḥ, spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ, kāyavijñānadhātuḥ; manodhātur, dharmadhātur, manovijñānadhātuḥ. eta ucyanta aṣṭādaśa dhātavaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_3] Therein, what are the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements)? Namely: the eye-element, the form-element, the eye-consciousness-element; the ear-element, the sound-element, the ear-consciousness-element; the nose-element, the smell-element, the nose-consciousness-element; the tongue-element, the taste-element, the tongue-consciousness-element; the body-element, the touch-element, the body-consciousness-element; the mind-element, the dharma-element, the mind-consciousness-element. These are called the eighteen <s>dhātus</s>.

body.text: [DsP_4] tatra katamāni catvāry āryasatyāni? yaduta duḥkham āryasatyaṃ, samudaya āryasatyaṃ, nirodha āryasatyaṃ, mārga āryasatyam. etāny ucyante catvāry āryasatyāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_4] Therein, what are the four Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>)? Namely: the Noble Truth of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the Noble Truth of the origin [of suffering] (<s>samudaya</s>), the Noble Truth of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and the Noble Truth of the path (<s>mārga</s>). These are called the four Noble Truths.

body.text: [DsP_5] tatra katamāni dvādaśa pratītyasamutpādāṅgāni? yadutāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapratyayāni ṣaḍ āyatanāni, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ, sparśapratyayā vedanā, vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā, tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam, upādānapratyayo bhavo, bhavapratyayā jātir, jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopayāsāḥ. evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati.
body.translated_text: [DsP_5] Therein, what are the twelve links of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>)? Namely: conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) arise volitional formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>); conditioned by volitional formations arises consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>); conditioned by consciousness arises name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>); conditioned by name-and-form arise the six sense bases (<s>ṣaḍ-āyatana</s>); conditioned by the six sense bases arises contact (<s>sparśa</s>); conditioned by contact arises feeling (<s>vedanā</s>); conditioned by feeling arises craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>); conditioned by craving arises clinging (<s>upādāna</s>); conditioned by clinging arises becoming (<s>bhava</s>); conditioned by becoming arises birth (<s>jāti</s>); conditioned by birth arise aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair. Thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering.

body.text: avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ, saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodho, vijñānanirodhān nāmarūpanirodho, nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ, ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ, sparśanirodhād vedanānirodho, vedanānirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhas, tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodha, upādānanirodhād bhavanirodho, bhavanirodhāj jātinirodho, jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopayāsanirodhaḥ. evam asya kevalasya duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati. eṣa ucyate pratītyasamutpādo 'nulomaś ca pratilomaś ca.
body.translated_text: From the cessation of ignorance comes the cessation of volitional formations; from the cessation of volitional formations comes the cessation of consciousness; from the cessation of consciousness comes the cessation of name-and-form; from the cessation of name-and-form comes the cessation of the six sense bases; from the cessation of the six sense bases comes the cessation of contact; from the cessation of contact comes the cessation of feeling; from the cessation of feeling comes the cessation of craving; from the cessation of craving comes the cessation of clinging; from the cessation of clinging comes the cessation of becoming; from the cessation of becoming comes the cessation of birth; from the cessation of birth comes the cessation of aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair. Thus there is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering. This is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), both in forward order (<s>anuloma</s>) and in reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>).

body.text: [DsP_6] tatra katamāni catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni? yaduta kāye kāyānupaśyanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ, vedanāsu vedanānupaśyanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ, citte cittānupaśyanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ, dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyanāsmṛtyupasthānam. etāny ucyante catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_6] Therein, what are the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)? Namely: the foundation of mindfulness consisting of contemplation of the body in the body (<s>kāye kāyānupaśyanā</s>), the foundation of mindfulness consisting of contemplation of feelings in feelings (<s>vedanāsu vedanānupaśyanā</s>), the foundation of mindfulness consisting of contemplation of mind in mind (<s>citte cittānupaśyanā</s>), and the foundation of mindfulness consisting of contemplation of dharmas in dharmas (<s>dharmeṣu dharmānupaśyanā</s>). These are called the four foundations of mindfulness.

body.text: [DsP_7] tatra katamāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni? iha bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nutpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām anutpādāya chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhati cittaṃ pragrhṇāti samyak pradadhāti;
body.translated_text: [DsP_7] Therein, what are the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)? Here, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> generates desire, strives, initiates energy, takes hold of the mind, and rightly applies it for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: utpannānāṃ pāpakānām akuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhati cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyak pradadhāti;
body.translated_text: Generates desire, strives, initiates energy, takes hold of the mind, and rightly applies it for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇām utpādāya chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhati cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyak pradadhāti;
body.translated_text: Generates desire, strives, initiates energy, takes hold of the mind, and rightly applies it for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye 'saṃpramoṣāya bhūyobhāvanāyai paripūraṇāya chandaṃ janayati vyāyacchate vīryam ārabhati cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti samyak pradadhāti. etāny ucyante catvāri samyakprahāṇāni.
body.translated_text: Generates desire, strives, initiates energy, takes hold of the mind, and rightly applies it for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. These are called the four right efforts.

body.text: [DsP_8] tatra katame catvāra ṛddhipādāh? yaduta chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipādo, vīryasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipādaś, cittasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhīpādo, mīmāṃsāsamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipādaḥ. eta ucyante catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_8] Therein, what are the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>)? Namely: the base of supernatural power endowed with the formative forces of concentration based on desire (<s>chanda</s>) and of abandonment; the base of supernatural power endowed with the formative forces of concentration based on energy (<s>vīrya</s>) and of abandonment; the base of supernatural power endowed with the formative forces of concentration based on mind (<s>citta</s>) and of abandonment; the base of supernatural power endowed with the formative forces of concentration based on investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>) and of abandonment. These are called the four bases of supernatural power.

body.text: [DsP_9] tatra katamāni pañcendriyāṇi? śraddhendriyaṃ, vīryendriyaṃ, smṛtīndriyaṃ, samādhīndriyaṃ, prajñendriyam. etāny ucyante pañcendriyāṇi.
body.translated_text: [DsP_9] Therein, what are the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>)? The faculty of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), the faculty of energy (<s>vīrya</s>), the faculty of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), the faculty of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and the faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). These are called the five faculties.

body.text: [DsP_10] tatra katamāni pañca balāni? śraddhābalaṃ, vīryabalaṃ, smṛtibalaṃ, samādhibalaṃ, prajñābalam. etāny ucyante pañca balāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_10] Therein, what are the five powers (<s>bala</s>)? The power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, and the power of wisdom. These are called the five powers.

body.text: [DsP_11] tatra katamāni sapta bodhyaṅgāni? yaduta smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ, dharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ, vīryasaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ, prītisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ, prasrabdhisaṃbodhyaṅgaṃ, samādhisaṃbodhyaṅgam, upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅgam. etāny ucyante sapta bodhyaṅgāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_11] Therein, what are the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>)? Namely: the awakening factor of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), the awakening factor of investigation of dharmas (<s>dharmapravicaya</s>), the awakening factor of energy (<s>vīrya</s>), the awakening factor of joy (<s>prīti</s>), the awakening factor of tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>), the awakening factor of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and the awakening factor of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). These are called the seven factors of awakening.

body.text: [DsP_12] tatra katama āryāṣṭāṅgamārgaḥ? yaduta samyagdṛṣṭiḥ, samyaksaṃkalpaḥ, samyagvāk, samyakkarmāntaḥ, samyagājīvaḥ, samyagvyāyāmaḥ, samyaksmṛtiḥ, samyaksamādhiḥ. eṣa ucyata āryāṣṭāngamārgaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_12] Therein, what is the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>)? Namely: right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). This is called the Noble Eightfold Path.

body.text: [DsP_13] tatra katamac chūnyatāvimokṣamukham? yaduta sarvadharmasvalakṣaṇatāśūnyapratyavekṣaṇacittasthitir vimokṣamukham. etad ucyate śūnyatāvimokṣamukham.
body.translated_text: [DsP_13] Therein, what is the door of liberation of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā-vimokṣamukha</s>)? Namely: the mental stability that consists of contemplating the emptiness of the own-characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s> is the door of liberation. This is called the door of liberation of emptiness.

body.text: [DsP_14] tatra katamad animittaṃ vimokṣamukham? yaduta sarvadharmasvalakṣaṇatānimittapratyavekṣaṇacittasthitir animittavimokṣamukham. etad ucyate 'nimittaṃ vimokṣamukham.
body.translated_text: [DsP_14] Therein, what is the signless door of liberation (<s>animitta-vimokṣamukha</s>)? Namely: the mental stability that consists of contemplating the signlessness of the own-characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s> is the signless door of liberation. This is called the signless door of liberation.

body.text: [DsP_15] tatra katamad apraṇihitaṃ vimokṣamukham? yaduta sarvadharmānabhisaṃskāre 'nabhisaṃskāracittasthitir apraṇihitavimokṣamukham. etad ucyate 'praṇihitaṃ vimokṣamukham.
body.translated_text: [DsP_15] Therein, what is the wishless door of liberation (<s>apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha</s>)? Namely: the mental stability of non-formation with respect to the non-formation of all <s>dharmas</s> is the wishless door of liberation. This is called the wishless door of liberation.

body.text: [DsP_16] tatra katamāni catvāri dhyānāni? yaduta viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati;
body.translated_text: [DsP_16] Therein, what are the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions)? Namely: secluded from sensual desires, secluded from evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), born of seclusion, accompanied by joy (<s>prīti</s>) and happiness (<s>sukha</s>), one enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>;

body.text: sa vitarkavicārāṇām upaśamād adhyātmaṃ saṃprasādāc cetasa ekotībhāvad avitarkam avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati;
body.translated_text: With the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, through inner tranquility and one-pointedness of mind, without applied thought and without sustained thought, born of concentration, accompanied by joy and happiness, one enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>;

body.text: sa prīter virāgād upekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānan, sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayati yat tad āryā ācakṣate smṛtimān sukhī sukhavihāry upekṣaka iti, niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati;
body.translated_text: With the fading away of joy, one abides in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body — that which the noble ones describe as 'equanimous, mindful, abiding in happiness' — one enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without joy;

body.text: sa sukhasya ca prahāṇād duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvam eva saumanasyadaurmanasyayor astaṃgamād aduḥkhāsukham upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharati. etāny ucyante catvāri dhyānāni.
body.translated_text: With the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering, and with the prior disappearance of elation and dejection, one enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. These are called the four <s>dhyānas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_17] tatra katamāni catvāry apramāṇāni? yaduta maitrī, karuṇā, muditā, upekṣā. etāny ucyante catvāry apramāṇāni.
body.translated_text: [DsP_17] Therein, what are the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>)? Namely: loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). These are called the four immeasurables.

body.text: [DsP_18] tatra katamāś catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ? yadutākāśānantyāyatanaṃ, vijñānānantyāyatanam, ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam. etā ucyante catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_18] Therein, what are the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpya-samāpatti</s>)? Namely: the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). These are called the four formless attainments.

body.text: [DsP_19] tatra katame 'ṣṭau vimokṣāḥ? yaduta rūpī rūpāṇi pasyaty, ayaṃ prathamo vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: [DsP_19] Therein, what are the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>)? Namely: possessing form, one sees forms — this is the first liberation;

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty, ayaṃ dvitīyo vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: Not perceiving internal form, one sees external forms — this is the second liberation;

body.text: śubham ity evādhimukto bhavaty, ayaṃ trtīyo vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: One becomes resolved upon the beautiful alone — this is the third liberation;

body.text: sa sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānām astaṃgamān nānātvasaṃjñānām amanasikārād anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaty, ayaṃ caturtho vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending all perceptions of form, by the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, by non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] 'space is infinite,' one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) — this is the fourth liberation;

body.text: sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānantaṃ vijñānam iti vijñānānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaty, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of infinite space, [thinking] 'consciousness is infinite,' one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>) — this is the fifth liberation;

body.text: sa sarvaśo vijñānānantyātanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiṃcid ity ākiñcanyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaty, ayaṃ ṣaṣṭho vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness, [thinking] 'there is nothing,' one enters and abides in the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) — this is the sixth liberation;

body.text: sa sarvaśa ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharaty,ayaṃ saptamo vimokṣaḥ;
body.translated_text: He completely transcends the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) and enters and abides in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — this is the seventh <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation);

body.text: sa sarvaśo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samatikramya saṃjñāvedayitanirodham upasaṃpadya viharaty, ayam aṣṭamo vimokṣaḥ. eta ucyante 'ṣṭau vimokṣāḥ.
body.translated_text: He completely transcends the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) and enters and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodha</s>) — this is the eighth <s>vimokṣa</s>. These are called the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations).

body.text: [DsP_20] tatra katamā navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ? yaduta
body.translated_text: [DsP_20] Therein, what are the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>)? Namely:

body.text: viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ prathamā samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: Secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome and unskillful <s>dharmas</s>, with applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) and sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>), he enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), born of seclusion, accompanied by joy and happiness — this is the first attainment;

body.text: sa vitarkavicārāṇām upaśamād adhyātmaṃ saṃprasādāc cetasa ekotībhāvād avitarkam avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ dvitīyā samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: With the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, through inner tranquility, through one-pointedness of mind, without applied thought, without sustained thought, he enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), accompanied by joy and happiness — this is the second attainment;

body.text: sa prīter virāgād upekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānan sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayati yat tad āryā ācakṣate smṛtimān sukhavihāry upekṣaka iti niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ tṛtīyā samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: With the fading away of joy, he abides in equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body. That of which the noble ones say 'He who is equanimous and mindful abides in happiness' — he enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, free from joy — this is the third attainment;

body.text: sa sukhasya ca prahāṇād duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvam eva saumanasyadaurmanasyayor astaṃgamād aduḥkhāsukham upeksāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ caturthī samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: With the abandoning of happiness and the abandoning of suffering, with the previous disappearance of mental pleasure and displeasure, he enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness — this is the fourth attainment;

body.text: sa sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramāt pratighasaṃjñānām astaṃgamān nānātvasaṃjñānām amanasikārād anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ pañcamī samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending all perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, by not attending to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] 'space is infinite,' he enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) — this is the fifth attainment;

body.text: sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānantaṃ vijñānam iti vijñānānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of infinite space, [thinking] 'consciousness is infinite,' he enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>) — this is the sixth attainment;

body.text: sa sarvaśo vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiṃcid ity ākiñcanyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ saptamī samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness, [thinking] 'there is nothing,' he enters and abides in the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) — this is the seventh attainment;

body.text: sa sarvaśa ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīyam aṣṭamī samāpattiḥ;
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of nothingness, he enters and abides in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — this is the eighth attainment;

body.text: sa sarvaśo naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ samatikramya saṃjñāvedayitanirodham upasaṃpadya viharatīyaṃ navamī samāpattiḥ. etā ucyante navānupūrvasamāpattayaḥ.
body.translated_text: By completely transcending the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he enters and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedayitanirodha</s>) — this is the ninth attainment. These are called the nine successive attainments.

body.text: [DsP_21] tatra katamā nava saṃjñāḥ? yaduta vidhmātakasaṃjñā, vipaḍumakasaṃjñā, vilohitakasaṃjñā, vipūyakasaṃjñā, vinīlakasaṃjñā, vikhāditakasaṃjñā, vikṣiptakasaṃjñā, asthikasaṃjñā, vidagdhakasaṃjñā. etā ucyante nava saṃjñāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_21] Therein, what are the nine perceptions (<s>saṃjñā</s>)? Namely: the perception of the bloated (<s>vidhmātakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the discolored (<s>vipaḍumakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the bloody (<s>vilohitakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the festering (<s>vipūyakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the blue-black (<s>vinīlakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the gnawed (<s>vikhāditakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the scattered (<s>vikṣiptakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the skeletal (<s>asthikasaṃjñā</s>), and the perception of the burnt (<s>vidagdhakasaṃjñā</s>). These are called the nine perceptions.

body.text: [DsP_22] tatra katamā daśānusmṛtayaḥ? yaduta buddhānusmṛtir, dharmānusmṛtiḥ, saṃghānusmṛtiḥ, śīlānusmṛtis, tyāgānusmṛtir, devatānusmṛtir, upaśamānusmṛtir, ānāpānānusmṛtiḥ, kāyagatānusmṛtir, maraṇānusmṛtiḥ. etā ucyante daśānusmṛtayaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_22] Therein, what are the ten recollections (<s>anusmṛti</s>)? Namely: recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>, recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, recollection of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), recollection of generosity (<s>tyāga</s>), recollection of the deities (<s>devatā</s>), recollection of tranquility (<s>upaśama</s>), recollection of breathing (<s>ānāpāna</s>), recollection directed toward the body (<s>kāyagatā</s>), and recollection of death (<s>maraṇa</s>). These are called the ten recollections.

body.text: [DsP_23] tatra katame ṣaṭ saṃjñākārāḥ? yadutānityasaṃjñā, duḥkhasaṃjñā, anātmasaṃjñā, aśubhasaṃjñā, maraṇasaṃjñā, sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñā. eta ucyante ṣaṭ saṃjñākārāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_23] Therein, what are the six aspects of perception (<s>saṃjñākāra</s>)? Namely: the perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of suffering (<s>duḥkhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of non-self (<s>anātmasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the unattractive (<s>aśubhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of death (<s>maraṇasaṃjñā</s>), and the perception of non-delight in the entire world (<s>sarvaloke 'nabhiratisaṃjñā</s>). These are called the six aspects of perception.

body.text: [DsP_24] tatra katamad dharmajñānam? yat pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ parikarmitatve paricchedajñānam idam ucyate dharmajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_24] Therein, what is knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmajñāna</s>)? That analytical knowledge which arises when the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) have been thoroughly cultivated — this is called knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_25] tatra katamad anvayajñānam? yac chakṣur anityam iti jñānam, evam eva śrotraṃ, ghrāṇaṃ, jihvā, kāyo, mano, rūpaṃ, śabdo, gandho, rasaḥ, spraṣṭavyaṃ, dharmā anityā iti yaj jñānam idam ucyate 'nvayajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_25] Therein, what is inferential knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>)? The knowledge that the eye is impermanent; likewise the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, the mind, form, sound, smell, taste, the tangible, and <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent — whatever knowledge [arises in this way], this is called inferential knowledge.

body.text: [DsP_26] tatra katamat paracittajñānam? yat parasattvānaṃ parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cetasi cetasikeṣu ca dharmeṣv avicikitsitaṃ jñānam idam ucyate paracittajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_26] Therein, what is knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>)? That undoubting knowledge of the minds and mental factors of other beings and other persons, [cognized] by mind alone — this is called knowledge of others' minds.

body.text: [DsP_27] tatra katamat saṃvṛtijñānam? yat pratipajjñānam idam ucyate saṃvṛtijñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_27] Therein, what is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñāna</s>)? That which is the knowledge of the path — this is called conventional knowledge.

body.text: [DsP_28] tatra katamad duḥkhajñānam? yad duḥkhasyotpādasthitijñānam idam ucyate duḥkhajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_28] Therein, what is knowledge of suffering (<s>duḥkhajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the arising and persistence of suffering — this is called knowledge of suffering.

body.text: [DsP_29] tatra katamat samudayajñānam? yat samudayasya prahāṇajñānam idam ucyate samudayajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_29] Therein, what is knowledge of origination (<s>samudayajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the abandoning of origination — this is called knowledge of origination.

body.text: [DsP_30] tatra kataman nirodhajñanam? yad duḥkhanirodhajñānam idam ucyate nirodhajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_30] Therein, what is knowledge of cessation (<s>nirodhajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the cessation of suffering — this is called knowledge of cessation.

body.text: [DsP_31] tatra kataman mārgajñānam? yad āryāṣṭāṅgamārgajñānam idam ucyate mārgajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_31] Therein, what is knowledge of the path (<s>mārgajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) — this is called knowledge of the path.

body.text: [DsP_32] tatra katamat kṣayajñānam? yad rāgadveṣamohakṣayajñānam idam ucyate kṣayajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_32] Therein, what is knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the destruction of desire, hatred, and delusion — this is called knowledge of destruction.

body.text: [DsP_33] tatra katamad anutpādajñānam? yad bhavagatyanutpadajñānam idam ucyate 'nutpādajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_33] Therein, what is knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>)? That knowledge of the non-arising of further existence and rebirth — this is called knowledge of non-arising.

body.text: [DsP_34] tatra katamad yathābhūtajñānam? yat tathāgatasya sarvajñatājñānam idam ucyate yathābhūtajñānam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_34] Therein, what is knowledge of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>)? That omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñatājñāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — this is called knowledge of things as they truly are.

body.text: [DsP_35] tatra katamad anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam? yac chaikṣāṇāṃ pudgalānām anabhisamitānāṃ śraddhendriyaṃ, vīryendriyaṃ, smṛtīndriyaṃ, samādhīndriyaṃ, prajñendriyaṃ idam ucyate 'nājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_35] Therein, what is the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>)? The faith-faculty (<s>śraddhendriya</s>), the energy-faculty (<s>vīryendriya</s>), the mindfulness-faculty (<s>smṛtīndriya</s>), the concentration-faculty (<s>samādhīndriya</s>), and the wisdom-faculty (<s>prajñendriya</s>) of those who are learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and who have not yet attained full realization — this is called the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown.'

body.text: [DsP_36] tatra katamad ājñendriyam? yac chaikṣāṇāṃ pudgalānām abhisamitānāṃ śraddhendriyaṃ vīryendriyaṃ, smṛtīndriyaṃ, samādhīndriyaṃ, prajñendriyam idam ucyate ājñendriyam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_36] Therein, what is the faculty of complete knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>)? The faith-faculty, the energy-faculty, the mindfulness-faculty, the concentration-faculty, and the wisdom-faculty of those who are learners and who have attained full realization — this is called the faculty of complete knowledge.

body.text: [DsP_37] tatra katamad ājñātāvīndriyam? yad aśaikṣāṇāṃ pudgalānāṃ tadyathārhatāṃ, pratyekabuddhānāṃ, daśabhūmisthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ, tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ śraddhendriyaṃ, vīryendriyaṃ, smṛtīndriyaṃ, samādhīndriyaṃ prajñendriyam idam ucyata ājñātāvīndriyam.
body.translated_text: [DsP_37] Therein, what is the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>)? The faith-faculty, the energy-faculty, the mindfulness-faculty, the concentration-faculty, and the wisdom-faculty of those who are beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), namely <s>arhats</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), <s>bodhisattvas</s> abiding on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), and <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones — this is called the faculty of one who has fully known.

body.text: [DsP_38] tatra katamaḥ savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhiḥ? viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya viharaty ayam ucyate savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhiḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_38] Therein, what is <s>samādhi</s> with applied and sustained thought (<s>savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ</s>)? Secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome and unskillful <s>dharmas</s>, he enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, accompanied by joy and happiness — this is called <s>samādhi</s> with applied and sustained thought.

body.text: [DsP_39] tatra katamo vitarko vicāramātraḥ samādhiḥ? yā prathamadhyānasya dvitīyadhyānasya cāntarikāyam ucyate 'vitarko vicāramātraḥ samādhiḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_39] Therein, what is <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought but with sustained thought only? That which is the intermediate state between the first <s>dhyāna</s> and the second <s>dhyāna</s> — this is called <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought but with sustained thought only.

body.text: [DsP_40] tatra katamo 'vitarko 'vicāraḥ samādhiḥ? prathamaṃ dhyānam upādāya yāvan naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattir eṣa ucyate 'vitarko 'vicāraḥ samādhiḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_40] Therein, what is <s>samādhi</s> without applied or sustained thought? Beginning from the first <s>dhyāna</s> up to the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — this is called <s>samādhi</s> without applied or sustained thought.

body.text: [DsP_41] tatra katamāny aṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni? yadutādhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni, tāni rūpāṇy abhibhūya jānāty abhibhūya paśyaty, evaṃsaṃjñī bhavatīdaṃ prathamam abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: [DsP_41] Therein, what are the eight bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>)? Namely: one who perceives form internally sees forms externally that are limited, whether beautiful or ugly; having mastered those forms, he knows and sees them — such is his perception — this is the first base of mastery;

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati mahadgatāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni, tāni rūpaṇy abhibhūya jānāty abhibhūya paśyaty, evaṃsaṃjñī bhavatīdaṃ dvitīyam abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: One who perceives formlessness internally sees forms externally that are extensive, whether beautiful or ugly; having mastered those forms, he knows and sees them — such is his perception — this is the second base of mastery;

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhāsāni, tadyathomāpuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā bāraṇaseyaṃ vastraṃ nīlaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ nīlanidarśanaṃ nīlanirbhāsam, evam evādhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhasānīdaṃ tṛtīyam abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: One who perceives formlessness internally sees forms externally that are blue, of blue color, blue in appearance, blue in luster — just as the <s>umā</s> flower is, or a fine <s>Bārāṇasī</s> cloth that is blue, of blue color, blue in appearance, blue in luster — in the same way, one who perceives formlessness internally sees forms externally that are blue, of blue color, blue in appearance, blue in luster — this is the third base of mastery;

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati pītāni pītavarṇāni pītanidarśanāni pītanirbhāsāni, tadyathā karṇikārapuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā bārāṇaseyaṃ vastraṃ pītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ pītanidarśanaṃ pītanirbhāsam, evam evādhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati pītāni pītavarṇāni pītanidarśanāni pītanirbhāsānīdaṃ caturtham abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: One who perceives formlessness internally sees forms externally that are yellow, of yellow color, yellow in appearance, yellow in luster — just as the <s>karṇikāra</s> flower is, or a fine <s>Bārāṇasī</s> cloth that is yellow, of yellow color, yellow in appearance, yellow in luster — in the same way, one who perceives formlessness internally sees forms externally that are yellow, of yellow color, yellow in appearance, yellow in luster — this is the fourth base of mastery;

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati lohitāni lohitavarṇāni lohitanidarśanāni lohitanirbhāsāni, tadyathā bandhujīvakapuṣpaṃ saṃpannaṃ vā bārāṇaseyaṃ vastraṃ lohitaṃ lohitavarṇaṃ lohitanidarśanaṃ lohitanirbhāsam, evam evādhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati lohitāni lohitavarṇāni lohitanidarśanāni lohitanirbhāsānīdaṃ pañcamam abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: Internally perceiving no form, one sees external forms that are red, of red color, of red appearance, of red radiance—just as a <s>bandhujīvaka</s> flower in full bloom, or a well-made Benares cloth that is red, of red color, of red appearance, of red radiance—even so, internally perceiving no form, one sees external forms that are red, of red color, of red appearance, of red radiance. This is the fifth <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (base of mastery).

body.text: adhyātmam arūpasaṃjnī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty avadātāny avadātavarṇāny avadātanidarśanāny avadātanirbhāsāni, tadyathośanastārakayā varṇo 'vadāto 'vadātavarṇo 'vadātanidarśano 'vadātanirbhāsa, evam evādhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyaty avadātāny avadātavarṇāny avadātanidarśanāny avadātanirbhāsānīdaṃ ṣaṣṭham abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: Internally perceiving no form, one sees external forms that are white, of white color, of white appearance, of white radiance—just as the star <s>Oṣaṇas</s> (Venus) is of white color, of white appearance, of white radiance—even so, internally perceiving no form, one sees external forms that are white, of white color, of white appearance, of white radiance. This is the sixth <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (base of mastery).

body.text: sa sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānaṃ samatikramat pratighasaṃjñānām astaṃgamān nānātvasaṃjñānām amanasikārād anantam ākāśam ity ākāśānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīdaṃ saptamam abhibhvāyatanam;
body.translated_text: Having completely transcended all perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, without attending to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] "space is infinite," one enters and abides in the base of the infinity of space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). This is the seventh <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (base of mastery).

body.text: sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānantaṃ vijñānam itī vijñānānantyāyatanam upasaṃpadya viharatīdam aṣṭamam abhibhvāyatanam. etāny ucyante 'ṣṭāv abhibhvāyatanāni.
body.translated_text: Having completely transcended the base of the infinity of space, [thinking] "consciousness is infinite," one enters and abides in the base of the infinity of consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). This is the eighth <s>abhibhvāyatana</s> (base of mastery). These are called the eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery).

body.text: [DsP_42] tatra katamāni daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni? yaduta pṛthivīkṛtsnam, apkṛtsnaṃ, tejaḥkṛtsnaṃ, vāyukṛtsnam, ākāśakṛtsnaṃ, nīlakṛtsnaṃ, pītakṛtsnaṃ, lohitakṛtsnam, avadātakṛtsnaṃ, vijñānakṛtsnam. etāny ucyante daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni:
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases)? They are: the totality of earth (<s>pṛthivīkṛtsna</s>), the totality of water (<s>apkṛtsna</s>), the totality of fire (<s>tejaḥkṛtsna</s>), the totality of wind (<s>vāyukṛtsna</s>), the totality of space (<s>ākāśakṛtsna</s>), the totality of blue (<s>nīlakṛtsna</s>), the totality of yellow (<s>pītakṛtsna</s>), the totality of red (<s>lohitakṛtsna</s>), the totality of white (<s>avadātakṛtsna</s>), and the totality of consciousness (<s>vijñānakṛtsna</s>). These are called the ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases).

body.text: sarvadhātūn pṛthivīdhātāv adhimucya sarvam api pṛthivīdhātur evaikadhātur bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into the earth element, everything becomes one single element, the earth element alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn abdhātāv adhimucya sarvam apy abdhātur evaikadhātur bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into the water element, everything becomes one single element, the water element alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūṃs tejodhātāv adhimucya sarvam api tejodhātur evaikadhātur bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into the fire element, everything becomes one single element, the fire element alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn vāyudhātāv adhimucya sarvam api vāyudhātur evaikadhātur bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into the wind element, everything becomes one single element, the wind element alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn ākāśadhātāv adhimucya sarvam apy ākāśadhātur evaikadhātur bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into the space element, everything becomes one single element, the space element alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn nīle dhimucya sarvam api nīlam eva bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into blue, everything becomes blue alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn pīte 'dhimucya sarvam api pītam eva bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into yellow, everything becomes yellow alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn lohite 'dhimucya sarvam api lohitam eva bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into red, everything becomes red alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn avadāte 'dhimucya sarvam apy avadātam eva bhavati;
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into white, everything becomes white alone.

body.text: sarvadhātūn vijñāne 'dhimucya sarvam api vijñānam evaikadhātur bhavati.
body.translated_text: By resolving all elements into consciousness, everything becomes one single element, consciousness alone.

body.text: pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśanīlapītalohitāvadātavijñānaṃ sarvam apy ekam eva bhavatīty etāny ucyante kṛtsnāyatanāni.
body.translated_text: Earth, water, fire, wind, space, blue, yellow, red, white, and consciousness—all become one. These are called the <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases).

body.text: nirantarakṛtsnaspharaṇād etāny ucyante kṛtsnāyatanāni. ekaikaṃ cāyatanaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati, tasmād ucyante kṛtsnāyatanānīti.
body.translated_text: Because of the uninterrupted total pervasion, these are called <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases). And each single base becomes everything; therefore they are called <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_43] tatra katamā aṣṭādaśa śūnyatāḥ? yadutādhyātmaśūnyatā, bahirdhāśūnyatā, adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā, śūnyatāśūnyatā, mahāśūnyatā, paramārthaśūnyatā, saṃskṛtaśūnyatā, asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā, atyantaśūnyatā, anavarāgraśūnyatā, anavakāraśūnyatā, prakṛtiśūnyatā, sarvadharmaśūnyatā, svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā, anupalambhaśūnyatā, abhāvaśūnyatā, svabhāvaśūnyatā, abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the eighteen <s>śūnyatās</s> (emptinesses)? They are: emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of the internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of intrinsic nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of own-nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamādhyātmaśūnyatā? ādhyātmikā dharmā ucyante, yaduta cakṣuḥ, śrotraṃ, ghrāṇaṃ, jihvā, kāyo, manaḥ. tatra cakṣuś cakṣuṣā śūnyam akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. evam eva śrotraṃ, ghrāṇaṃ, jihvā, kāyo, mano manasā śūnyam akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'dhyātmaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>)? Internal <s>dharmas</s> are said to be the eye, the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, and the mind. Therein, the eye is empty of the eye, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). Likewise, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind—the mind is empty of the mind, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā bahirdhāśūnyatā? bāhyā dharmā ucyante yaduta rūpaṃ, śabdo, gandho, rasaḥ, spraṣṭavyaṃ, dharmāḥ. tatra rūpāṇi rūpaiḥ śūnyāny akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. evam eva śabdo, gandho, rasaḥ, spraṣṭavyaṃ, dharmā dharmaiḥ śūnyā akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate bahirdhāśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>)? External <s>dharmas</s> are said to be form, sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, and <s>dharmas</s> [as mental objects]. Therein, forms are empty of forms, since [they are] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. Likewise, sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, and <s>dharmas</s> are empty of <s>dharmas</s>, since [they are] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā? adhyātmabāhyā dharmā ucyante ṣaḍ ādhyātmikāny āyatanāni, ṣaḍ bāhyāny āyatanāni. tatrādhyātmikā dharmā ādhyātmikair dharmaiḥ śūnyā akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. bāhyā dharmā bāhyair dharmaiḥ śūnyā akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'dhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>)? Internal and external <s>dharmas</s> are said to be the six internal sense bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) and the six external sense bases. Therein, internal <s>dharmas</s> are empty of internal <s>dharmas</s>, since [they are] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. External <s>dharmas</s> are empty of external <s>dharmas</s>, since [they are] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā śūnyatāśūnyatā? yā sarvadharmaśūnyatā tayā sarvadharmaśūnyatayā sarvadharmaśūnyatā śūnyākūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>)? That which is the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>—by that emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> is empty, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature.

body.text: tatra katamā mahāśūnyatā? pūrvā dik pūrvayā diśā śūnyākūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. evam eva dakṣiṇā, paścimā, uttarā dik, catasro vidiśas, tā aṣṭau diśa, uparisṭāddig upariṣṭāddiśā śūnyā, adhastāddig adhastāddiśā śūnyākūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate mahāśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>)? The eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. Likewise, the southern, western, and northern directions, the four intermediate directions—those eight directions—the upward direction is empty of the upward direction, and the downward direction is empty of the downward direction, since [they are] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. This is called the great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā paramārthaśūnyatā? paramārtha ucyate nirvāṇam. tatra nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇena śūnyam akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate paramārthaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>)? The ultimate reality is said to be <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Therein, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is empty of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā? saṃskṛtam ucyate kāmadhātū, rūpadhātur, arūpadhātuḥ. tatra kāmadhātuḥ kāmadhātunā śūnyo 'kūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya. evam eva rūpadhātū rūpadhātunā śūnyo, 'rūpadhātur arūpadhātunā śūnyaḥ; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate saṃskṛtaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>)? The conditioned is said to be the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), and the formless realm (<s>arūpadhātu</s>). Therein, the desire realm is empty of the desire realm, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Likewise, the form realm is empty of the form realm, and the formless realm is empty of the formless realm. Why is that? Because this is their intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamāsaṃskṛtaśūnyatā? asaṃskṛtam ucyate yasya dharmasya notpādo, na sthitir, na nirodho, nānyathātvam. tatrāsaṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtena śūnyam akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'saṃskṛtaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>)? The unconditioned is said to be that <s>dharma</s> of which there is no arising, no abiding, no cessation, and no alteration. Therein, the unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamātyantaśūnyatā? yasya dharmasya notpāda upalabhyate 'kūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'tyantaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the ultimate emptiness (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>)? That <s>dharma</s> whose arising is not apprehended, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the ultimate emptiness (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamānavarāgraśūnyatā? yasya dharmasya nāgatir upalabhyate 'kūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'navarāgraśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>)? That <s>dharma</s> whose destination is not apprehended, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamānavakāraśūnyatā? yatra na kasyacid dharmasyāvakāro 'kūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'navakāraśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>)? Where there is no rejection of any <s>dharma</s>, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā prakṛtiśūnyatā? yā sarvadharmāṇāṃ prakṛtiḥ saṃskṛtānāṃ vāsaṃskṛtānāṃ vā sā na śrāvakaiḥ kṛtā, na pratyekabuddhaiḥ kṛtā, na bodhisattvaiḥ kṛtā, na buddhair bhagavadbhiḥ kṛtākūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate prakṛtiśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of intrinsic nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>)? The intrinsic nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, whether conditioned or unconditioned—it was not made by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, nor made by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, nor made by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, nor made by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, since [it is] neither permanent nor subject to destruction. Why is that? Because this is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of intrinsic nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: tatra katamā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā? tatra rūpyalakṣaṇaṃ rūpam, anubhavalakṣaṇā vedanā, saṃjānanalakṣaṇā saṃjñā, abhisaṃskāralakṣaṇāḥ saṃskārāḥ, vijānanalakṣaṇaṃ vijñānaṃ peyālaṃ yāvad yac ca saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yac cāsaṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ sarva ete dharmāḥ svena svena lakṣaṇena śūnyā akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of specific characteristics? Therein, <s>rūpa</s> (form) has the characteristic of materiality, <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) has the characteristic of experiencing, <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) has the characteristic of apprehending, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) have the characteristic of conditioning, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) has the characteristic of cognizing—and so on in abbreviated form up to—whatever is the characteristic of conditioned <s>dharmas</s> and whatever is the characteristic of unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>, all these <s>dharmas</s> are empty of their own specific characteristics, taking into account that they are neither eternally fixed nor subject to annihilation. Why is that? Because this is their nature. This is called the emptiness of specific characteristics.

body.text: tatra katamā sarvadharmaśūnyatā? sarvadharmā ucyante pañca skandhā, dvādaśāyatanāny, aṣṭādaśa dhātavo, rūpiṇo dharmā, arūpiṇo dharmāḥ, saṃskṛtā dharmā, asaṃskṛtā dharmāḥ. tatra sarvadharmāḥ sarvadharmaiḥ śūnyā akūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate sarvadharmaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>? All <s>dharmas</s> are said to be the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements), material <s>dharmas</s>, immaterial <s>dharmas</s>, conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, and unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of all <s>dharmas</s>, taking into account that they are neither eternally fixed nor subject to annihilation. Why is that? Because this is their nature. This is called the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatra katamānupalambhaśūnyatā? sāpi sarvadharmānupalambho 'kūṭasthāvināśitām upādāya; tat kasmād dhetoḥ? prakṛtir asyaiṣā. iyam ucyate 'nupalambhaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of non-apprehension? That too is the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, taking into account that they are neither eternally fixed nor subject to annihilation. Why is that? Because this is their nature. This is called the emptiness of non-apprehension.

body.text: tatra katamābhāvaśūnyatā? yatra na kaścid bhāva upalabhyata iyam ucyate 'bhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of non-existence? That wherein no existence whatsoever is apprehended—this is called the emptiness of non-existence.

body.text: tatra katamā svabhāvaśūnyatā? yaḥ sāṃyogikasya svabhāvābhāva iyam ucyate svabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of intrinsic nature? That which is the absence of intrinsic nature in what is composite—this is called the emptiness of intrinsic nature.

body.text: tatra katamābhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā? nāsti sāṃyogikasya kaścit svabhāvaḥ. iyam ucyate 'bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence? There is no intrinsic nature whatsoever in what is composite. This is called the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

body.text: punar aparaṃ śāradvatīputra bhāvo bhāvena śūnyo, 'bhāvo 'bhāvena śūnyaḥ, svabhāvaḥ svabhāvena śūnyaḥ, parabhāvaḥ parabhāvena śūnyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, existence is empty of existence, non-existence is empty of non-existence, intrinsic nature is empty of intrinsic nature, and other-nature is empty of other-nature.

body.text: tatra katamo bhāvaḥ? bhāva ucyate pañca skandhā yaduta rūpaṃ, vedanā, saṃjñā, saṃskārā, vijñānam. tatra bhāvo bhāvena śūnyaḥ.
body.translated_text: Therein, what is existence? Existence is said to be the five <s>skandhas</s>, namely <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Therein, existence is empty of existence.

body.text: katham abhāvo 'bhāvena śūnyaḥ? abhāva ucyate 'saṃskṛtam. tatrāsaṃskṛtam asaṃskṛtena śūnyam, evam abhāvo 'bhāvena śūnyaḥ.
body.translated_text: How is non-existence empty of non-existence? Non-existence is said to be the unconditioned. Therein, the unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned. Thus non-existence is empty of non-existence.

body.text: kathaṃ svabhāvaḥ svabhāvena śūnyaḥ? yā sarvadharmāṇāṃ śūnyatā sā na jñānena kṛtā na darśanena kṛtā na kenacit kṛtā. ayaṃ svabhāva ucyate svabhāvena śūnyaḥ.
body.translated_text: How is intrinsic nature empty of intrinsic nature? The <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of all <s>dharmas</s> is not made by knowledge, not made by vision, not made by anyone. This is called intrinsic nature, and it is empty of intrinsic nature.

body.text: kathaṃ parabhāvaḥ parabhāvena śūnyaḥ? yotpādād vā tathāgatānām anutpādād vā tathāgatānāṃ sthitaivaiṣā dharmāṇāṃ dharmasthititā, dharmadhātur, dharmānavadyatā, tathatāviparyāsatathatānanyatathatā, bhūtakoṭir yaś cemeṣāṃ pareṇa śūnyaḥ parabhāvaḥ sa ucyate parabhāvena śūnyaḥ.
body.translated_text: How is other-nature empty of other-nature? Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not arise, this very <s>dharmasthititā</s> (stable nature of dharmas) of <s>dharmas</s> remains established—the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma), the irreproachability of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), non-reversed suchness, non-other suchness, the ultimate point of reality. That which is empty of these by what is other—that other-nature is said to be empty of other-nature.

body.text: ete śāradvatīputra te sarvadharmā yeṣv anabhiniviṣṭo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pāraṃ gataḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyate.
body.translated_text: These, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are all those <s>dharmas</s> with regard to which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, being non-grasping, has gone to the far shore of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and quickly attains <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening).

body.text: daśasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā nidānaparivarto nāma prathamaḥ.
body.translated_text: The first chapter of the <s>Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, called the <s>Nidāna</s> Chapter (Introduction).

body.text: daśasāhasrikā prajñāpāramitā, dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ.
body.translated_text: <s>Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the Second Chapter.

body.text: [DsP_44] tato bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram avocat: tatra katamāni śāradvatīputra tathāgatasya daśa balāni? yaduta
body.translated_text: [DsP_44] Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: "Therein, what, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? Namely:

body.text: sthānaṃ sthānato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāty asthānam asthānato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is what is possible as possible and what is impossible as impossible;

body.text: atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ karmaṇāṃ karmasamādānānāṃ ca sthānaśo hetuśo vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the ripening of past, future, and present actions and undertakings of actions, with respect to their conditions and causes;

body.text: anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the world with its many and diverse elements;

body.text: sa parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ nānādhimuktikatām anekādhimuktikatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the diverse and manifold inclinations of other beings and other persons;

body.text: parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānām indriyaparāparatvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the superior and inferior faculties of other beings and other persons;

body.text: sarvatragāminīṃ pratipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the practice that leads everywhere;

body.text: indriyabalabodhyaṅgavimokṣadhyānasamādhisamāpattīnāṃ saṃkleśavyavadānavyutthānajñānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the defilement, purification, and emergence regarding the faculties, powers, factors of awakening, liberations, <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and attainments;

body.text: anekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsam anusmarati;
body.translated_text: He recollects many kinds of previous abodes;

body.text: sattvānāṃ cyutyupapattiṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti;
body.translated_text: He knows as it truly is the passing away and rebirth of beings;

body.text: āsravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāsravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñāya sākṣātkṛtyopasaṃpadya viharati: kṣīnā me jātir, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti. imāni śāradvatīputra tathāgatasya daśa balāni.
body.translated_text: Through the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows), he dwells having realized by his own direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having attained and entered upon it: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, I know there is no further existence beyond this.' These, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: [DsP_45] tatra katamāni śāradvatīputra catvāri vaiśāradyāni?
body.translated_text: [DsP_45] Therein, what, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, are the four kinds of fearlessness?

body.text: samyaksaṃbuddhasya me pratijānata ime dharmā anabhisaṃbuddhā ity atra vata māṃ śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā kaścid vā punar loke saha dharmeṇa codayed iti nimittam etan na samanupaśyāmi, nimittam etad aham asamanupaśyan kṣemaprāpto viharāmy abhayaprāpto vaiśāradyaprāpto viharāmy, udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānāṃ pratijānāmi, parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi, brāhmaṃ cakraṃ pravartayāmy apravartitapūrvaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā kenacid vā loke saha dharmeṇeti;
body.translated_text: When I, as one fully awakened, declare 'these <s>dharmas</s> have been fully awakened by me,' I do not see any ground on which any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, any <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world could legitimately challenge me. Not seeing such a ground, I dwell having attained security, having attained fearlessness, having attained confidence.
