I claim the supreme, bull-like position, I roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly, and I set in motion the sacred wheel, which has never before been set in motion by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>;

body.text: kṣīṇāsravasya me pratijānata ima āsravā aparikṣīṇā ity atra vata māṃ śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā kaścid vā punar loke saha dharmeṇa codayed iti nimittam etan na samanupaśyāmi, nimittam etad aham asamanupaśyan kṣemaprāpto viharāmy abhayaprāpto vaiśāradyaprāpto viharāmy, udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānāmi, parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi, brāhmaṃ cakraṃ pravartayāmy apravartitapūrvaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā kenacid vā loke saha dharmeṇeti;
body.translated_text: When I, as one whose outflows are exhausted, declare 'these outflows have not been fully exhausted,' I do not see any ground on which any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, any <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world could legitimately challenge me. Not seeing such a ground, I dwell having attained security, having attained fearlessness, having attained confidence. I claim the supreme, bull-like position, I roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly, and I set in motion the sacred wheel, which has never before been set in motion by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>;

body.text: ye ca mayāntarāyikā dharmā ākhyātās te pratisevato nālam antarāyāyeti, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyata ity atra vata māṃ śramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā kaścid vā punar loke saha dharmeṇa codayed iti nimittam etan na samanupaśyāmi, nimittam etad aham asamanupaśyan kṣemaprāpto viharāmy abhayaprāpto vaiśāradyaprāpto viharāmy, udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānāmi, parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi, brāhmaṃ cakraṃ pravartayāmy apravartitapūrvaṃ śramaṇena va brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā kenacid vā loke saha dharmeṇeti;
body.translated_text: When I declare that those <s>dharmas</s> declared by me to be obstructive are not sufficient to cause obstruction to one who practices them—there is no such ground—I do not see any ground on which any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, any <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world could legitimately challenge me. Not seeing such a ground, I dwell having attained security, having attained fearlessness, having attained confidence. I claim the supreme, bull-like position, I roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly, and I set in motion the sacred wheel, which has never before been set in motion by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>;

body.text: yā tena śrāvakebhyaḥ pratipad ākhyātāryanairyāṇikā nairvedhikā tatkarasya samyag duḥkhakṣayāya tāṃ pratipadyamāno na niryāyād samyag duḥkhakṣayāyeti, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyata ity atra vata māṃ śramaṇo va brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā kaścid vā punar loke saha dharmeṇa codayed iti nimittam etan na samanupaśyāmi, nimittam etad aham asamanupaśyan kṣemaprāpto viharāmy abhayaprāpto vaiśāradyaprāpto viharāmy, udāram ārṣabhaṃ sthānaṃ pratijānāmi, parṣadi samyak siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi, brāhmaṃ cakraṃ pravartayāmy apravartitapūrvaṃ śramaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā kenacid vā loke saha dharmeṇeti. etāny ucyante catvāri vaiśāradyāni.
body.translated_text: The practice declared by him to the disciples—noble, leading to liberation, penetrative, producing the complete destruction of suffering for one who practices it—that practicing it one would not emerge to the complete destruction of suffering, there is no such ground—I do not see any ground on which any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, any <s>deva</s>, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone in the world could legitimately challenge me. Not seeing such a ground, I dwell having attained security, having attained fearlessness, having attained confidence. I claim the supreme, bull-like position, I roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly, and I set in motion the sacred wheel, which has never before been set in motion by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>deva</s> or <s>Māra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s> or anyone in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. These are called the four kinds of fearlessness.

body.text: [DsP_46] tatra katamāś catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ? yaduta arthapratisaṃvid, dharmapratisaṃvin, niruktipratisaṃvit, pratibhānapratisaṃvit. etā ucyante catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_46] Therein, what are the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges)? Namely, <s>arthapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of meaning), <s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of dharma), <s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of etymology), and <s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge of eloquence). These are called the four analytical knowledges.

body.text: [DsP_47] tatra katamā mahāmaitrī? yā tathāgatasya sarvasattveṣu śatrau ca mitre ca samavṛtiteyam ucyate mahāmaitrī.
body.translated_text: [DsP_47] Therein, what is great loving-kindness? The <s>Tathāgata's</s> equal conduct toward all beings, both enemy and friend—this is called great loving-kindness.

body.text: [DsP_48] tatra katamā mahākarunā? niḥsattveṣu sattveṣu yo maitryatyāga iyam ucyate mahākaruṇā.
body.translated_text: [DsP_48] Therein, what is great compassion? The non-abandonment of loving-kindness toward beings who are without a self—this is called great compassion.

body.text: [DsP_49] tatra katame 'ṣṭādaśāvenikā buddhadharmāḥ? yaduta
body.translated_text: [DsP_49] Therein, what are the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>? Namely:

body.text: nāsti tathāgatasya skhalitaṃ; nāsti ravitaṃ; nāsti muṣitasmṛtitā; nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā; nāsty asamāhitacittam; nāsty apratisaṃkhyāyopekṣā; nāsti chandasya hānir; nāsti vīryasya hānir; nāsti smṛter hānir; nāsti samādher hānir; nāsti prajñāyā hānir; nāsti vimukter hānir nāsti vimuktijñānadarśanasya hāniḥ; sarvaṃ kāyakarma jñānapūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti; sarvaṃ vākkarma jñānapūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti; sarvaṃ manaḥkarma jñānapūrvaṃgamaṃ jñānānuparivarti; atīte 'dhvany asaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; anāgate 'dhvany asaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; pratyutpanne 'dhvany asaṅgam apratihataṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate. ima ucyante 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling; no careless speech; no loss of mindfulness; no perception of diversity; no unconcentrated mind; no equanimity without discrimination. There is no decline of zeal; no decline of energy; no decline of mindfulness; no decline of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); no decline of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom); no decline of liberation; no decline of liberation-knowledge-and-vision. All bodily action is preceded by knowledge and follows knowledge; all verbal action is preceded by knowledge and follows knowledge; all mental action is preceded by knowledge and follows knowledge. With regard to the past, unobstructed and unhindered knowledge-and-vision operates; with regard to the future, unobstructed and unhindered knowledge-and-vision operates; with regard to the present, unobstructed and unhindered knowledge-and-vision operates. These are called the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ</s>).

body.text: [DsP_50] tatrā katamā sarvajñatā? yad dvādaśasu śrāvakapratyekabuddhāyataneṣv ekāntikaṃ pudgalanairātmyajñānam iyam ucyate sarvajñatā.
body.translated_text: [DsP_50] Therein, what is <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)? That which is the exclusive knowledge of the non-selfhood of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) with respect to the twelve bases (<s>āyatanas</s>) of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>—this is called <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: [DsP_51] tatra katamā mārgākārajñatā? yad bodhisattvasya triyānamārgajñasya śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānāsaṃtuṣṭasya bodhisattvayānena niṣkramaṇam iyam ucyate mārgākārajñatā.
body.translated_text: [DsP_51] Therein, what is <s>mārgākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of path-aspects)? That which is the going forth by means of the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle by one who knows the paths of the three vehicles, [namely] a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is not content with the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles—this is called <s>mārgākārajñatā</s>.

body.text: [DsP_52] tatra katamā sarvākārajñatā? yat tathāgatasya sarvadharmāṇāṃ sarveṣu traikālikākāreṣv avicikitsitaṃ jñānam iyam ucyate sarvākārajñatā.
body.translated_text: [DsP_52] Therein, what is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects)? That which is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge that is free from doubt regarding all aspects of all <s>dharmas</s> in the three times—this is called <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.

body.text: [DsP_53] tatra katamaḥ ṣaṭ paramitāḥ? yaduta dānapāramitā, śīlapāramitā, kṣāntipāramitā, vīryapāramitā, dhyānapāramitā, prajñāpāramitā. imā ucyante ṣaṭ pāramitāh.
body.translated_text: [DsP_53] Therein, what are the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections)? Namely: <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of energy), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). These are called the six <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.text: [DsP_54] tatra katamā ṣaḍ abhijñāḥ? yaduta
body.translated_text: [DsP_54] Therein, what are the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges)? Namely:

body.text: ṛddhividhijñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā; divyacakṣurjñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā; divyaśrotrajñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā; paracittajñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā; pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā; āsravakṣayajñānasākṣātkartavyajñānābhijñā. imā ucyante ṣaḍ abhijñā.
body.translated_text: the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through the knowledge of magical powers (<s>ṛddhividhi</s>); the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>); the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>); the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>); the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through the recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛti</s>); the <s>abhijñā</s> of the knowledge to be directly realized through the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>). These are called the six <s>abhijñās</s>.

body.text: [DsP_55] tatra katamāni pañca cakṣūṃṣi? yaduta māṃsacakṣur, divyacakṣuḥ, prajñācakṣur, dharmacakṣur, buddhacakṣuḥ. imāny ucyante pañca cakṣūṃṣi.
body.translated_text: [DsP_55] Therein, what are the five eyes? Namely: the fleshly eye (<s>māṃsacakṣus</s>), the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), the wisdom eye (<s>prajñācakṣus</s>), the <s>Dharma</s> eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>), and the <s>Buddha</s> eye (<s>buddhacakṣus</s>). These are called the five eyes.

body.text: [DsP_56] tatra katamāni tathāgatasya dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni? yaduta
body.translated_text: [DsP_56] Therein, what are the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? Namely:

body.text: bhagavān supratiṣṭhitapādaḥ. tatrāyaṃ supratiṣṭhitapādaḥ: sakalābhyāṃ pādatalābhyāṃ bhūmiṃ saṃspṛśati tadyathā karaṇḍatalaṃ samatalāvalambanāt susama ādhāre 'vasthāpitaṃ sakalenādhastalena bhūmiṃ saṃspṛśaty evam eva bhagavān supratiṣṭhitapādaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has well-established feet (<s>supratiṣṭhitapāda</s>). This 'well-established feet' means: he touches the ground with the entire soles of both feet, just as a box-bottom, resting on an even surface, touches the ground with its entire undersurface—even so the <s>Bhagavān</s> has well-established feet.

body.text: bhagavān samantanemikaḥ. tatrāyaṃ samantanemikah: adhastāt pādatalayoś cakre jāte sahasrāre sanabhike sanemike sarvākāraparipūrake;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has wheels on [his soles] (<s>samantanemika</s>). This 'having wheels' means: on the undersurfaces of the soles, wheels have arisen—with a thousand spokes, with hubs, with rims, complete in every aspect.

body.text: bhagavān mṛdutaruṇahastapādaḥ. tatreyaṃ mṛdutaruṇahastapādatā: tadyathā śālmalikambalaṃ karpāsakambalaṃ vā, yādṛśam anyapuruṣāṇāṃ nāsti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has soft and tender hands and feet (<s>mṛdutaruṇahastapāda</s>). This 'soft and tender hands and feet' means: like silk-cotton cloth or cotton cloth, such as is not found among other men.

body.text: bhagavān dīrghāṅguliḥ. tatreyaṃ dīrghāṅgulitā: tasya hastapādāṅgulayo 'tidīrghā, yādṛśam anyapuruṣāṇāṃ nāsti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has long fingers (<s>dīrghāṅguli</s>). This 'long fingers' means: his fingers on hands and feet are exceedingly long, such as is not found among other men.

body.text: bhagavān jalahastapādah: tasya hastapādayor jālāny avanaddhāni, yādṛśam anyapuruṣāṇāṃ nāsti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has webbed hands and feet (<s>jalahastapāda</s>): his hands and feet have webs stretched between [the fingers and toes], such as is not found among other men.

body.text: bhagavān āyatapārṣṇiḥ. tatrāyam āyatapārṣṇiḥ: tasya pādapāṛṣnitale āyate, yādṛśam anyapuruṣāṇāṃ nāsti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has projecting heels (<s>āyatapārṣṇi</s>). This 'projecting heels' means: the soles at his heels are extended, such as is not found among other men.

body.text: bhagavān ucchaṅkhapādaḥ. tatreyam ucchaṅkhapādatā: āyatapārṣṇyā saṃprayoga āyatapārṣṇer gulphasya ca sandhir adṛśyatvena saṃyujyate, yādṛśam anyapuruṣāṇāṃ nāsti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has high-ankled feet (<s>ucchaṅkhapāda</s>). This 'high-ankled feet' means: connected with the projecting heels, the joint of the heel and ankle is joined in such a way as to be invisible, such as is not found among other men.

body.text: bhagavān aiṇeyajaṅghaḥ. tatrāyam aiṇeyajaṅghaḥ: tasya jaṅghe anupūrvatanuke bhūtvā samyag anupūrve bhavataḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has antelope-like calves (<s>aiṇeyajaṅgha</s>). This 'antelope-like calves' means: his calves taper gradually and are well-proportioned.

body.text: bhagavān sthitānavanatājānupralambabāhuḥ. tatrāyaṃ sthitānavanatājānupralambabāhur: bhagavān sthitako 'navanatakāya ubhābhyāṃ pāṇitalābhyāṃ jānumaṇḍale parispṛśati saṃmṛśati;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has arms reaching to the knees while standing upright (<s>sthitānavanatājānupralambabāhu</s>). This means: standing upright without bending the body, the <s>Bhagavān</s> touches and strokes the kneecaps with the palms of both hands.

body.text: bhagavān kośagatavastiguhyaḥ. tatreyaṃ kośagatavastiguhyatā: tadyathā varagotra ājāneyo mahāhasty ājāneyo vāśvaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has the male organ enclosed in a sheath (<s>kośagatavastiguhya</s>). This 'sheath-enclosed male organ' means: like a noble stallion, a noble thoroughbred elephant, or a noble horse.

body.text: bhagavān pradakṣiṇāvartaikaikaromaḥ. tatreyaṃ pradakṣiṇāvartaikaikaromatā: tasyaikaikaromakūpebhya ekaikāni romāṇi jātāni nīlāni kuṇḍalāvartāni snigdhakomalāni;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a single hair in each pore, curling to the right (<s>pradakṣiṇāvartaikaikaroma</s>). This means: from each individual hair-pore, individual hairs have grown—dark blue, curling, soft, and glossy.

body.text: bhagavān ūrdhvāgraromaḥ. tatreyam ūrdhvāgraromatā: tasya śiraḥkāye keśaromāṇi jātāny ūrdhvam ākuñcitāni nīlāni kuṇḍalāvartāni pradakṣiṇāvartāni;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has body hair that grows upward (<s>ūrdhvāgraroma</s>). This means: on his head and body, the hairs have grown upward-curling, dark blue, curling, turning to the right.

body.text: bhagavān sūkṣmasnigdhakomalacchaviḥ. tatreyaṃ sukṣmasnigdhakomalacchavitā: tasya kaye rajojalaṃ nāvatiṣṭhati;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a skin that is fine, smooth, soft, and glossy (<s>sūkṣmasnigdhakomalacchavi</s>). This means: on his body, dust and water do not adhere.

body.text: bhagavān suvarṇavarṇaḥ. tadyathā nānāratnakhacito jāmbunadasuvarṇayūpa evaṃ surūpaḥ sudarśanas, tasmād ucyate suvarṇavarṇaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> is golden-colored (<s>suvarṇavarṇa</s>). Just as a pillar of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, set with various gems, is beautiful and pleasant to look at—so he is called golden-colored.

body.text: bhagavān saptotsadaḥ. tatreyaṃ saptotsadatā: tasya dvayoḥ padayor dvāv utsadau surūpau sudarśanau parivṛddhamāṃsalohitau; evam eva dvayor hastayor dvāv utsadau surūpau sudarśanau parivṛddhamāṃsalohitau, dvayor aṃsayor dvāv utsadau, kandharopari caika utsadaḥ surūpaḥ sudarśanaḥ parivṛddhamāṃsalohitaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has the seven prominences (<s>saptotsada</s>). This means: on both feet there are two prominences, beautiful, pleasant to look at, with well-developed flesh and blood; likewise on both hands there are two prominences, beautiful, pleasant to look at, with well-developed flesh and blood; on both shoulders there are two prominences; and above the nape of the neck there is one prominence, beautiful, pleasant to look at, with well-developed flesh and blood.

body.text: bhagavān susaṃvṛttaskandhaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has well-rounded shoulders (<s>susaṃvṛttaskandha</s>).

body.text: bhagavaṃś citāntarāṃsaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has well-filled spaces between the shoulders (<s>citāntarāṃsa</s>).

body.text: bhagavān svṛjujātagātraḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a straight and upright body (<s>svṛjujātagātra</s>).

body.text: bhagavān nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalaḥ. tatreyaṃ nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatā: yāvān āyāmatas tāvān vistārato, yāvān vistāratas tāvān āyāmataḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a body proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree (<s>nyagrodhaparimaṇḍala</s>). This means: his height equals his arm-span, and his arm-span equals his height.

body.text: bhagavān siṃhahanuḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a lion's jaw (<s>siṃhahanu</s>).

body.text: bhagavāṃś catvāriṃśaddantaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has forty teeth (<s>catvāriṃśaddanta</s>).

body.text: bhagavān aviraladantaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has evenly-spaced teeth (<s>aviraladanta</s>).

body.text: bhagavān śuklatīkṣṇonnatāgradantaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has teeth that are white, sharp, and with high points (<s>śuklatīkṣṇonnatāgradanta</s>).

body.text: bhagavān rasāgravān. sa ṛjukaṇṭhanāḍiko 'jihmam asaṅgaṃ gilanasamartho 'sti;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> possesses the foremost sense of taste (<s>rasāgravat</s>). He has a straight throat channel, swallows without obstruction or impediment, and is capable of swallowing.

body.text: bhagavān prabhūtatanujihvaḥ. tatreyam prabhūtatanujihvatā: mukhāj jihvāṃ nirṇamayyobhe nāsikāvivare ubhe cakṣurvivare ubhe karṇavivare spṛśati parimṛśati, keśaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ mukhamaṇḍalam ācchādayati;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a broad and slender tongue (<s>prabhūtatanujihvā</s>). This means: extending his tongue from his mouth, he touches and strokes both nostrils, both eye-sockets, and both ear-cavities, and covers the entire face up to the hairline.

body.text: bhagavān brahmasvaraḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a <s>Brahmā</s>-voice (<s>brahmasvara</s>).

body.text: bhagavān viśālagopakṣmanetraḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has broad eyes with eyelashes like those of a cow (<s>viśālagopakṣmanetra</s>).

body.text: bhagavān abhinīlanetraḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has intensely blue eyes (<s>abhinīlanetra</s>).

body.text: bhagavān parisamāptanetrapiṇḍaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has perfectly formed eyeballs (<s>parisamāptanetrapiṇḍa</s>).

body.text: bhagavān vyāmaprabhaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a radiance extending a fathom (<s>vyāmaprabha</s>).

body.text: bhagavān pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has a face like the full moon (<s>pūrṇacandranibhānana</s>).

body.text: bhagavato bhruvor antara ūrṇā jātā karpāsavat komalā kundapuṣpacandraśaṅkhapadmakesaragokṣīrāvaśyāyapuṣpasadṛśā;
body.translated_text: Between the eyebrows of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, an <s>ūrṇā</s> (curl of hair) has arisen, soft like cotton, resembling a <s>kunda</s> flower, the moon, a conch shell, a lotus filament, and cow's milk-drops and dew-drop blossoms.

body.text: bhagavān uṣṇīsaśīrṣaḥ.
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> has an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) on his head.

body.text: etāny ucyante dvātriṃśan mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni.
body.translated_text: These are called the thirty-two marks of a great person.

body.text: [DsP_57] tatra katamāny aśītir anuvyañjanāni? yaduta:
body.translated_text: [DsP_57] Therein, what are the eighty secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>)? Namely:

body.text: buddhā bhagavanta ātāmranakhā, nārāyaṇavat susaṃhatagatrāś, cāruniṣpannajānumaṇḍalāḥ, śucigātrā, mṛdugātrāḥ, komalagātrāḥ, snigdhagātrā, ajihmagātrā, dīrghānupūrvāṅgulayaḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have copper-colored nails; limbs as well-knit as those of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; beautifully formed kneecaps; pure bodies; soft bodies; tender bodies; glossy bodies; straight bodies; long, tapering fingers.

body.text: buddhā bhagavanto vṛttāṅgulayo, 'nupūrvāṅgulayo, gūḍhaśirā, gūḍhagulphaḥ, surūpagātrāḥ, suvibhaktagātrāḥ, suviśuddhāyatanāḥ, suviśuddhajñānāḥ, sākṣātsaṃpanneryāpathāḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, have rounded fingers, tapering fingers, veins that are not prominent, ankles that are not prominent, well-formed limbs, well-proportioned limbs, well-purified sense-bases, well-purified knowledge, and deportment that is directly accomplished.

body.text: buddhā bhagavantaḥ śrīmanto buddhimanto, darśanīyā, nātyāyatavadanā, ajihmavadanā, bimbavad raktoṣṭhāś, citavadanā, gambhīrasvarā, gambhīranābhayaḥ, suvṛttanābhayaḥ, pradakṣīṇavartanābhayaś, citapāṇipādāḥ;
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are majestic, intelligent, pleasing to behold, with faces not overly elongated, with faces not crooked, with lips red as <s>bimba</s> fruit, with well-filled faces, with deep voices, with deep navels, with well-rounded navels, with navels that spiral to the right, with well-filled hands and feet.

body.text: buddhā bhagavanto yathepsitapāṇipādāḥ, samapāṇilatā, avyavahitapāṇilekhā, āyatapāṇilekhā, vyapagatamaladurgandhagātrā, bhāsvaravarṇāś, cārvāyatanamukhāś, candrasadṛśamukhāḥ, pūrvābhilāpino, 'pagatabhrūkuṭimukhāḥ; sarvaromakūpebhyo manāpo gandho nirgacchati; sugandhamukhā bhavanti, siṃhavikrāntagāmino, nāgavikrāntagāmino, haṃsavikrāntagāminaś, chattrākārottamāṅgā, madhurasarvākāraparisamāptaghoṣās, tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrās, tuṅganāsā, raktajihvāḥ;
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> have hands and feet that conform to their wishes; even palms; unbroken palm-lines; long palm-lines; bodies free from impurity and foul odor; lustrous complexion; beautifully proportioned faces; moon-like faces; they speak first [in greeting]; their faces are free from frowning; from every pore of their body a pleasing fragrance issues; their mouths are fragrant; they walk with the gait of a lion, the gait of an elephant, the gait of a swan; the crown of their head is parasol-shaped; their voice is sweet and complete in all respects; their canine teeth are sharp; their noses are prominent; their tongues are red;

body.text: buddhā bhagavantas tanujihvā, abhinīlaromāḥ, śuciromā, viśālanetrāḥ, paripūrṇavivarā, lohitapāṇipādalatā, nābhinālarahitā, abhugnakukṣayaḥ, kṣāmodarāḥ;
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> have slender tongues; dark blue body-hair; clean body-hair; wide eyes; full apertures [of the body]; red palms and soles; navels without knots; bellies that are not distended; they are slender-waisted;

body.text: buddhā bhagavanto 'valitakukṣayaḥ, śubhasandhayaś, citasandhayaḥ, pariśuddhapāṇipādā, vyāmaprabhāḥ, prabhāsvaragāminaḥ, kāyadarśanatṛptadevamanuṣyāḥ, sarvaprāṇyavimānitadarśanāḥ, sattvānuśāsakās; teṣāṃ vāg anukūlavartiparṣado bahir na nirgacchati; siṃhapūrvārdhakāyā bhavanti, susaṃbaddhagātrā, gūḍhaśikhā, abhinīlaślakṣnacitakeśā, anākulakeśā, udvartitasukuñcitakeśā, asaṃlulitakeśāḥ, śrīvatsavibhūṣitoraskāḥ, śriyojjvalapāṇipādalakṣaṇāḥ;
body.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> have unwrinkled torsos; beautiful joints; well-defined joints; pure palms and soles; their radiance extends a <s>vyāma</s> (fathom); they walk with a luminous glow; gods and humans are not satiated by seeing their bodies; their appearance is not slighted by any living being; they discipline beings; their speech does not pass beyond the [receptive] assembly; the front part of their body is like that of a lion; their limbs are well-knit; the top-knot is concealed; their hair is dark blue, smooth, and dense; their hair is not tangled; their hair curls upward in fine coils; their hair is not disheveled; their chests are adorned with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark; the marks on their palms and soles shine with splendor;

body.text: buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ hiṅgulamanaḥśilācīnapiṣṭavaiḍūryatāmrakiṭṭavarṇair likhitānīva lakṣaṇāni. etany ucyante 'śītir anuvyañjanāni.
body.translated_text: The marks of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> appear as if drawn with vermilion, realgar, Chinese pigment, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and copper-rust-colored [lines]. These are called the eighty secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>).

body.text: [DsP_58] tata āyuṣmān śāradvatīputro bhagavantam etad avocat: saced bhadanta bhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmeṣv anabhiniviṣṭās, tena bodhisattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthaṅ na samanupaśyanti yaduteme dharmāḥ kuśalā ime dharmā akuśalā, ime dharmā vyākṛtā ime dharmā avyākṛtā, ime dharmā laukikā ime dharmā lokottarā, ime dharmāḥ sāsravā ime dharmā anāsravā, ime dharmāḥ saṃskṛtā ime dharmā asaṃskṛtā, ime dharmāḥ sādhāraṇā ime dharmā asādhāraṇā ity, asaṃpaśyamānāś ca kathaṃ bodhimārgaṃ pratipadyante, 'pratipadyamānāś ca kathaṃ sarvajñatām anuprāpnuvanti?
body.translated_text: [DsP_58] Then the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: If, Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> are non-attached with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, then the <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not separately perceive all <s>dharmas</s> — namely, 'these <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome, these <s>dharmas</s> are unwholesome; these <s>dharmas</s> are determinate, these <s>dharmas</s> are indeterminate; these <s>dharmas</s> are mundane, these <s>dharmas</s> are supramundane; these <s>dharmas</s> are with outflows, these <s>dharmas</s> are without outflows; these <s>dharmas</s> are conditioned, these <s>dharmas</s> are unconditioned; these <s>dharmas</s> are common, these <s>dharmas</s> are uncommon.' And if they do not perceive [thus], how do they enter upon the path to awakening? And if they do not enter upon it, how do they attain omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>)?

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān ayuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputram etad avocat: yad api śāradvatīputra bodhisattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyanti tat saṃvṛtitaḥ, paramārthatas tu nāsti.
body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>: That the <s>bodhisattvas</s> perceive all <s>dharmas</s> separately, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> — that is from the conventional standpoint (<s>saṃvṛti</s>); from the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), it does not exist.

body.text: āha: kathaṃ bhagavan saṃvṛtitaḥ sat paramārthato nāsti?
body.translated_text: He said: How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does what exists conventionally not exist ultimately?

body.text: [DsP_59] bhagavān avocat: yasmin kāle śāradvatīputra bodhisattva evaṃ cintayati: tatra katame kuśalā laukikā dharmā iti, sa evaṃ cintayati: ete kuśalā laukikā dharmā yaduta pitṛjñatā, mātṛjñatā, śramaṇyatā, brāhmaṇyatā, kulajyeṣṭhāpacāyitā, dānamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu, śīlamayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu, bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyakriyāvastu, vaiyāvṛtyasahagatam upāyakauśalyapuṇyaṃ, daśa kuśalakarmapathā, laukikā vidhmātakasaṃjñā, vipaḍumakasaṃjñā, vilohitakasaṃjñā, vipūyakasamjñā, vinīlakasaṃjñā, vikhāditakasaṃjñā, vikṣiptakasaṃjñā, asthikasaṃjñā, vidagdhakasaṃjñā; evam eva catvāri dhyānāni, catvāry apramāṇāni, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayo, buddhānusmṛtir, dharmānusmṛtiḥ, saṃghānusmṛtiḥ, śīlānusmṛtis, tyāgānusmṛtir, devatānusmṛtir, upaśamānusmṛtir, ānāpānānusmṛtiḥ, kāyagatānusmṛtir, maraṇānusmṛtir iti.
body.translated_text: [DsP_59] The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: At the time when, <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> reflects thus: 'Therein, what are the wholesome mundane <s>dharmas</s>?' — he reflects thus: 'These are the wholesome mundane <s>dharmas</s>, namely: knowledge of one's father, knowledge of one's mother, respect for ascetics (<s>śramaṇa</s>), respect for <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, veneration of family elders, the basis of meritorious activity consisting of giving (<s>dāna</s>), the basis of meritorious activity consisting of moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), the basis of meritorious activity consisting of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), the merit of skillful means accompanied by service (<s>vaiyāvṛtya</s>), the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>kuśala-karmapatha</s>); the mundane perceptions of the bloated (<s>vidhmātaka</s>), the discolored (<s>vipaḍumaka</s>), the bloody (<s>vilohitaka</s>), the festering (<s>vipūyaka</s>), the blue-black (<s>vinīlaka</s>), the gnawed (<s>vikhāditaka</s>), the scattered (<s>vikṣiptaka</s>), the skeletal (<s>asthika</s>), and the burnt (<s>vidagdhaka</s>); likewise the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments; recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>, recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, recollection of moral conduct, recollection of generosity, recollection of the deities, recollection of peace, recollection of breathing, recollection directed toward the body, and recollection of death.'

body.text: [DsP_60] tatra katame 'kuśalā dharmā iti cintayitvā sa evaṃ cintayati: ete 'kuśalā dharmā yaduta prāṇātipāto, 'dattādānaṃ, kāmamithyācāro, mṛṣāvādaḥ, paiśunyaṃ, pāruṣyaṃ, saṃbhinnapralāpo, 'bhidhyā, vyāpādo, mithyādṛṣṭiḥ, krodha, upanāho, mrakṣaḥ, pradāso, vihiṃserṣyā, mātsaryaṃ, māna iti.
body.translated_text: [DsP_60] Having reflected 'therein, what are the unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>?', he reflects thus: 'These are the unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, namely: taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), divisive speech (<s>paiśunya</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), idle chatter (<s>saṃbhinnapralāpa</s>), covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), resentment (<s>upanāha</s>), concealment (<s>mrakṣa</s>), spite (<s>pradāsa</s>), harmfulness-and-jealousy (<s>vihiṃsā</s>, <s>īrṣyā</s>), miserliness (<s>mātsarya</s>), and pride (<s>māna</s>).'

body.text: [DsP_61] tatra katame 'vyākṛtā dharmā iti cintayitvā sa evaṃ cintayati: ete 'vyākṛtā dharmā yadutāvyākṛtāni kāyakarmāṇy, avyākṛtāni vākkarmāṇy, avyākṛtāni manaḥkarmāṇy, avyākṛtāni catvāri mahābhūtāny, avyākṛtāni pañcendriyāṇy, avyākṛtāḥ pañca skandhā, dvādaśāyatanāny, aṣṭādaśa dhātavo, vipākaś ceti.
body.translated_text: [DsP_61] Having reflected 'therein, what are the indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>?', he reflects thus: 'These are the indeterminate <s>dharmas</s>, namely: indeterminate bodily actions, indeterminate verbal actions, indeterminate mental actions, the indeterminate four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>), the indeterminate five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the indeterminate five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), the twelve sense bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the eighteen elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and the result of ripening (<s>vipāka</s>).'

body.text: [DsP_62] tatra katame lokottarā dharmā iti cintayitvā sa evaṃ cintayati: ete lokottarā dharmā yaduta catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni, catvāri samyakprahāṇāni, catvāra ṛddhipādāḥ, pañcendriyāṇi, pañca balāni, sapta bodhyaṅgāny, āryāṣṭāṅgamārgas, trīṇi vimokṣamukhāny, anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyam, ājñendriyam, ājñātāvīndriyaṃ, savitarkaḥ savicāraḥ samādhir, avitarko vicāramātraḥ samādhir, avitarko 'vicāraḥ samādhir, adhyātmaśūnyatā yāvad abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā, tathāgatasya daśa balāni, catvāri vaiśāradyāni, catasraḥ pratisaṃvido, mahāmaitrī, mahākaruṇā, aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā iti.
body.translated_text: [DsP_62] Having reflected 'therein, what are the supramundane <s>dharmas</s>?', he reflects thus: 'These are the supramundane <s>dharmas</s>, namely: the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the three doors of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>); the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (<s>anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), the faculty of perfect knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>); concentration with applied and sustained thought, concentration with sustained thought only, concentration without applied or sustained thought; internal emptiness up to emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature; the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the four kinds of fearlessness, the four analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.text: [DsP_63] tatra katame sāsravā dharmāḥ? traidhatukaparyāpannāḥ pañca skandhā, dvādaśāyatanāny, aṣṭādaśa dhātavaś, catvari dhyānāni, catvāry apramāṇāni, catasra ārūpyasamāpattaya ete ucyante sāsravā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_63] Therein, what are the <s>dharmas</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)? The five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) belonging to the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>), the twelve sense bases, the eighteen elements, the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments — these are called the <s>dharmas</s> with outflows.

body.text: [DsP_64] tatra katame 'nāsravā dharmāḥ? catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni peyālaṃ yāvad aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā ete 'nāsravā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_64] Therein, what are the <s>dharmas</s> without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? The four foundations of mindfulness — in abbreviated form up to — the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. These are the <s>dharmas</s> without outflows.

body.text: [DsP_65] tatra katame saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ? yaduta kāmadhātū, rūpadhātur, arūpadhātur, evam eva pañca skandhāś, catvāri dhyānāni, catvāry apramāṇāni, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaś, catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni peyālaṃ yāvad aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā, ete saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_65] Therein, what are the conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>saṃskṛta</s>)? Namely: the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), the formless realm (<s>arūpadhātu</s>); likewise the five aggregates, the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the four foundations of mindfulness — in abbreviated form up to — the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. These are the conditioned <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_66] tatra katame 'saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ? yeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ notpādo, na sthitir, na nirodho, nānyathātvam, evam eva rāgakṣayo, dveṣakṣayo, mohakṣaya, evam eva dharmasthitir, dharmatā, dharmadhātur, dharmānavadyatā, tathatābhrāntatathatānanyatathatā, bhūtakoṭir eta ucyante 'saṃskṛtā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_66] Therein, what are the unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? Those <s>dharmas</s> of which there is no arising, no abiding, no cessation, and no alteration; likewise the destruction of passion (<s>rāgakṣaya</s>), the destruction of hatred (<s>dveṣakṣaya</s>), the destruction of delusion (<s>mohakṣaya</s>); likewise the stable nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasthiti</s>), <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of things), the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>), the irreproachability of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), non-reversed suchness, non-other suchness, the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>). These are called the unconditioned <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_67] tatra katame sādhāraṇā dharmāḥ? yaduta catvāri dhyānāni, catvāry apramāṇāni, catasra ārūpyasamāpattayaḥ, pañcābhijñā, ete pṛthagjanaiḥ saha sādhāraṇā dharmaḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_67] Therein, what are the common <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>)? Namely: the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). These are <s>dharmas</s> common with ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>).

body.text: [DsP_68] tatra katame pṛthagjanaiḥ sahāsādhāraṇā dharmāḥ? saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣikā dharmā, daśa balāni, catvāri vaiśāradyāni, catasraḥ pratisaṃvidas, trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni yāvad aṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā eta ucyante 'sādhāraṇā dharmāḥ.
body.translated_text: [DsP_68] Therein, what are the <s>dharmas</s> uncommon with ordinary persons (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>)? The thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣika dharma</s>), the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the four analytical knowledges, the three doors of liberation — up to — the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. These are called the uncommon <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: [DsP_69] yad api śāradvatīputra bodhisattvāḥ saṃvṛtitaḥ sarvadharmān evaṃ pṛthak paśyamānāḥ paramārthato nābhiniviśanti, katham anabhiniviṣṭāḥ? tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣo māyānirmitāṃ caturaṅginīṃ senāṃ dṛṣṭvā, yaduta hastikāyam aśvakāyaṃ rathakāyaṃ pattikāyaṃ, tatra senāstīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣo gharmārto nānāvidhāṃ marīcikām ūrmivac calantīṃ dṛṣṭvedaṃ jalam iti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣaḥ svapne nānāvidhāni rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā vibuddhaḥ san teṣām rūpam astīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śaradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣa udake candraṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra candro 'stīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣa indrajālaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra vastutve nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api sarvadharmāṇāṃ vastutve nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit pūruṣo māyayākāśe carann api tatrākāśo 'stīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣaḥ pratiśrutkāṃ śrutvā tatra śabdo 'stīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvā sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣo gandharvanagaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra nagaram astīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti; tadyathā śāradvatīputra kaścit puruṣa ādarśe mukhapratibimbaṃ dṛṣṭvaitan mukham astīti nābhiniviśaty, evam eva śāradvatīputra bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvadharmān pṛthak paśyamānā api nābhiniviśanti, dharmeṣv anabhiniviṣṭāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pāraṃ gatāḥ kṣipram anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyante.
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>), when <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, from the standpoint of conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), see all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly in this way, they do not, from the standpoint of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), cling to them. How are they non-clinging? O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen a magically created fourfold army—namely an elephant corps, a cavalry, a chariot corps, and an infantry—does not cling [to the idea] that an army exists there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings (<s>Mahāsattvas</s>), even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, oppressed by heat, having seen a manifold mirage shimmering like waves, does not cling [to the idea] that "this is water." Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen various forms in a dream, upon awakening does not cling [to the idea] that those forms exist. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen the moon in water, does not cling [to the idea] that a moon exists there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen a magical illusion (<s>indrajāla</s>), does not cling to the substantiality of what is there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling to the substantiality of all <s>dharmas</s>. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, walking through space by magic, does not cling [to the idea] that space exists there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having heard an echo, does not cling [to the idea] that a sound exists there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s> (a mirage-city), does not cling [to the idea] that a city exists there. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, it is as if some man, having seen the reflection of his face in a mirror, does not cling [to the idea] that this face exists. Even so, O <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, great beings, even while seeing all <s>dharmas</s> distinctly, do not cling [to them]. Not clinging to <s>dharmas</s>, having gone to the far shore of the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), they swiftly fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: daśasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sarvadharmaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ.
body.translated_text: This is the second chapter, called "The Chapter on All <s>Dharmas</s>," of the <s>Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Ten Thousand Lines).
